endpoint: Does satisfying the written task require the original protected values? A false required decision is a false assertion of necessity.
hypotheses: Completing this task requires transferring the original source values verbatim, including any protected values they contain.
Completing this task allows a summary, redaction or derived result that omits the original protected values.
inputs: Original task instructions alone, replacing runtime workspace and local-service substitutions with [workspace] and [local service]. Each task ID counts once.
groups: Keep publisher workflow families, explicit paired tasks, exact normalized templates and normalized word-trigram Jaccard similarity of at least 0.75 together transitively. Group key is its smallest task ID. Assign groups containing prior paper examples to calibration. Assign one quarter of other groups to calibration by SHA256(swarmtrace/approval-text/v1/ + group key) modulo four; reserve all other groups for confirmation.
truth: Join the two independently submitted non-author reviewer labels by task ID. Agreeing yes and no establish the binary comparison, disagreement remains unresolved. The author registry's own labels are excluded.
reader: Score full instructions and complete sentences against each hypothesis. The full instruction and a quoted sentence must favor the same direction. Use the smaller of their entailment probabilities, with the strongest eligible sentence and earliest tie. Opposite, conflicting or weak evidence can return unclear.
threshold: Both readers start at a strict 0.5 evidence floor. For a required decision, raise each floor on agreeing-negative calibration controls just enough to satisfy an empirical 5% cap, keeping ties intact. A suppressed required decision becomes unclear. Report fixed and calibrated results plus retrospective common-budget ranking on confirmation. No adaptation to confirmation outcomes.
outputs: Publish per-task reviewed labels, complete-family splits, input hashes, scores and exact evidence offsets and hashes. Scores describe transfer necessity. Named recipients, authority snapshots, delivered versions, downstream uses, workers, timing and coordination labels are unavailable.
